newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE says Serbia must reinstate opposition wins.
newsitem.headline: OSCE says Serbia must reinstate opposition wins.

text.p: Europe's top security forum urged Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic on Tuesday to reinstate opposition victories in disputed local polls immediately, after Milosevic climbed down in the face of mass protests.

"The OSCE (Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe) hopes this move by Milosevic will result in the immediate reinstatement of the election results," an OSCE spokeswoman in Vienna told Reuters.
"The OSCE notes that while this would be a first step, further steps towards democratisation and dialogue with the opposition are essential," she added.
Thousands of Serbians have protested for the past 78 days since the Socialist Party annulled opposition victories in 14 major cities and towns on November 17, citing unspecified "irregularities".
Milosevic two days ago sent in the much-feared security police to break up protests in the capital Belgrade, provoking criticism from the Vienna-based OSCE.

"The authorities in Belgrade have recently resorted to the use of force and arrests in order to prevent the opposition from peaceful demonstrations. The chairman-in-office must express his deep concern and dismay at this development," Danish Foreign Minister and OSCE chairman Niels Helveg Petersen said in a statement earlier on Tuesday.

The official Yugoslav news agency Tanjug later reported that Milosevic had done an about-turn and written to Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic, instructing him to have parliament uphold the poll results.

"In keeping with its constitutional competence, I propose that the Serbian government submit to parliament a draft emergency law which will proclaim as final results of a part of local elections in Serbia in keeping with the findings of the OSCE mission," Milosevic was quoted as saying.
The OSCE backed a report made recently by former Spanish premier Felipe Gonzalez who visited Serbia on behalf of the organisation to study the polls and found the opposition had won in the 14 cities.
The OSCE said that recognising the results of the election was an essential step for the resolution of the crisis in Serbia.
"The original results of the election need to be translated into seats. In the OSCE context, new laws are not necessary for that," the spokeswoman said.
